intended_object: The presheaf of rings on a manifold M whose sections over an open set U are the ring of smooth (C^∞) functions U → R, where R is a smooth ring, with restriction maps as transition maps. This comes from the docstring and from the module, where it is the underlying presheaf of `smoothSheafRing`.
explanation:
The value on an open set U is the type of sections of `smoothSheaf IM I M R` over U. By definition, this is `C^∞⟮IM, U; I, R⟯`, the type of smooth maps U → R. The ring structure on it is the pointwise one, taken from `ContMDiffMap`. The map attached to an inclusion V ≤ U is restriction, packaged as a ring homomorphism by `ContMDiffMap.restrictRingHom`. The functor laws (`map_id`, `map_comp`) hold by `rfl`. This is exactly the standard presheaf of smooth R-valued functions, viewed as a presheaf of rings.

The setting is general. The source only needs to be a charted space over any model with corners, over any nontrivially normed field. The target R can be any ring with a smooth ring structure (`ContMDiffRing I ∞ R`).

Two restrictions are design choices, not narrowings:
- M and R must live in the same universe. This is the usual constraint when working in the category `RingCat.{u}`.
- The smoothness order is fixed at ∞. This matches the base sheaf `smoothSheaf`.

The analogous presheaves of groups and commutative groups follow the same pattern. Mathlib has no more general version of this construction elsewhere; this declaration is itself the Mathlib one.
